liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **// Turn On Your Lovelight (reel #2 side B; 8-track 15 ips)** (2 reviews): Listener notes blistering solos throughout the performance of this song; Listener loves the lead guitar solo in this performance [10][14]
- **Death Don't Have No Mercy (reel #2 side B; 8-track 15 ips)** (2 reviews): Listener describes this performance as hot; Listener uses this track to demonstrate Pigpen's keyboard abilities [13][16]
- **Good Morning Little School (reel #2 side B; 8-track 15 ips)** (1 review): Listener highlights blistering solos during the performance of this song [10]
- **New Potato Caboose (reel #1 side A; 2-track 7.5 ips)** (1 review): Listener likes this performance, noting it contains some great jamming [13]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): Pigpen plays an organ solo that the listener describes as being on fire [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Cryptical**: rare: 12 archived performances [17]
- **Cryptical (reel #1 side B; 8-track 15 ips)**: rare: 12 archived performances [17]
- **Caution // has cut**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **end crowd (reel #1 side A; 2-track 7.5 ips)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1967-11-11.116172.sbd.motb-0173.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 14 songs; 95 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [1]
- **gd67-11-11.sbd.sacks.1613.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 58 min; rated 4.27/5 by 15 [4]. Said about its sound: Listener calls it the best sounding 1967 recording they have heard; Listener considers this track the best performance of the song in their opinion; Sound quality becomes muddy on tracks four through seven of the recording [6][8]
- **gd1967-11-11.116369.sbd.motb-0173.flac24**: soundboard; 14 songs; 95 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1967-11-11.141133.sbd.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: soundboard; 7 songs; 70 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- Listener questions if Tom Constanten played organ, noting he joined later in 1968 [8]
- Listener clarifies the jam occurred in the Shrine Exposition Hall, not the auditorium [9]
- Pigpen played keyboards, as Tom Constanten did not join the band until 1968 [11]
- Band had not yet started playing Born Cross-eyed, which first appeared in 1968 [13]
- Listener recalls riding a bike near the Pacific Ocean while listening to this jam [14]
- Blog post identifies the venue as Shrine Exhibition Hall in Los Angeles [19]
- Recording starts a few seconds into the song, which was new to the band [23]
- Listener compares the energy favorably to the March 18, 1967 Winterland show [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1967-11-11.116172.sbd.motb-0173.flac16**: taped by Dan Healy; transferred by Transfer By: Matt Smith & Bob Menke Mastering By: Derek McCabe; source: Updated [1]
- **gd67-11-11.sbd.sacks.1613.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Kirby (Chalupa) Bell; source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1967-11-11.116369.sbd.motb-0173.flac24**: taped by Dan Healy; transferred by Transfer By: Matt Smith & Bob Menke Mastering By: Derek McCabe; source: Updated [2]
- **gd1967-11-11.141133.sbd.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: 8 Track Master Reel > 1st Gen Reel (7.5ips) > PCM (Sony Beta ESXHiFi/L-750) - Given to Tim Dalton by Bob Menke; Transfer: PCM > Sony SL-10 > Sony… [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by David Seabury Grateful Dead: [1967-11-11 Shrine Exposition Hall, Los Angeles, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1967-11-11-shrine-auditorium-los-angeles-ca-usa/) [20]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Shrine Exhibition Hall, LA, Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1967/artwork/shrine-exhibition-hall-la-poster) [22]
